item.title: Lake Park students compete for Ms. ABAC crown
item.description: Twenty-four contestants will compete in Abraham Baldwin Agricultural College’s 56th annual Ms. ABAC Pageant on Feb. 26.

item.title: Republican Pridemore not running for reelection to PSC
item.description: A Republican incumbent on the Georgia Public Service Commission announced Tuesday that she will not stand for reelection, just months after two Democrats ejected two GOP incumbents with decisive electoral victories.

item.title: SRTC, Kennesaw State sign new articulation agreement for early childhood education program
item.description: Southern Regional Technical College and Kennesaw State University have signed a comprehensive articulation agreement that creates a clear academic pathway for students pursuing careers in education.

item.title: Valdosta state Rep. Sharper set to plead guilty to pandemic unemployment fraud
item.description: Another Democratic state legislator, state Rep. Dexter Sharper, is expected to plead guilty to COVID-19 unemployment fraud charges.

item.title: JAMES CAGLE: We all have two sets of eyes
item.description: We all have two sets of eyes. We have physical eyes and then we have what is called the mind’s eye. The physical eyes have sight and perceive the material world. The mind’s eye has insight and perceives things intellectually and spiritually.

item.title: Georgia Power says it can reduce electricity bills despite storm damage repair costs
item.description: Georgia's main electric power monopoly filed requests with state regulators Tuesday to set new billing rates for customers that will recover the cost of storm-related repairs and adjust for changes in fuel prices.

item.title: Boys & Girls Club of South Georgia celebrates new name with ribbon cutting
item.description: The Boys & Girls Club of South Georgia marked a new chapter with a ribbon cutting ceremony hosted by the Valdosta-Lowndes Chamber of Commerce.

item.title: ‘Marisol’: VSU ready to open dark, surreal comedy
item.description: Dr. Melissa Rynn Porterfield calls “Marisol” a “mixed bag of fun and terror.”
